root_cause: The deployment cube path validates that referenced metric nodes and dimension attributes exist, but the per-cube validation does not fail a cube when one of its declared dimensions is absent from the dimension-link graph of a metric's ultimate non-metric parent. As a result, `dj push` can create or update a syntactically valid cube whose metric parent transforms cannot join to every declared dimension, leaving the failure to surface later during SQL generation.
approach: In bulk cube validation, resolve each metric to its unique ultimate non-metric parent revisions, then build one batched dimension reachability map for all cube parent revisions and declared cube dimension node names. In per-cube validation, check each declared dimension attribute, including role-qualified references, against every parent revision used by the cube metrics and append INVALID_DIMENSION errors for missing paths before creating the cube revision. Keep the existing existence/status validation and cube metadata construction unchanged.
tests_to_add: Unit test DimensionReachability role-aware unreachable checks, including bare references that should not match role-only paths
Deployment orchestrator regression test where a cube references an existing dimension attribute that is not reachable from one metric parent and is marked INVALID with an actionable error
risk_notes: Role-qualified dimension links and local dimensions need exact matching so valid self-dimensions and role-specific joins are not rejected; derived metrics with multiple parents should require reachability from every resolved parent.
out_of_scope_observations: Direct REST cube creation already calls shared-dimension validation; this plan is limited to the `dj push` deployment validation path.
